title: Excellence of a scheme is detected on an affine open cover
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ be a covering by affine open subschemes such that every ring $\mathcal O_X(U_i)$ is excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Then for every affine open subscheme $V\subseteq X$ the ring $\mathcal O_X(V)$ is excellent. In particular every open subscheme of $X$ is again covered by affine opens with excellent rings.

source.place: Tag 0HAB (lemma-locally-excellent), implication (3) implies (2), and its final sentence; uses Tag 0HAA (lemma-characterize-excellent) and Properties lemma-locally-G-scheme

proof.text: Put $A_i=\mathcal O_X(U_i)$. By [def-exc-excellent-ring], each excellent $A_i$ is Noetherian, a G-ring, J-2, and universally catenary. The given affine cover by Noetherian rings witnesses that $X$ is locally Noetherian by the definition [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Thus the locally Noetherian hypothesis needed below has been established from the actual hypotheses, without assuming quasi-compactness.

source.place: Tag 0HAB (lemma-locally-excellent), proof via the component predicates; Tag 07QT (more-algebra.tex, definition-excellent) and Tag 01OV (properties.tex, definition-noetherian).

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary affine open $V\subseteq X$ and write $B=\mathcal O_X(V)$. Apply [lem-trf-g-ring-affine-cover] to the original cover and the G-ring property of each $A_i$ from step 1. Its conclusion gives that $B$ is a G-ring. In particular $B$ is Noetherian, as included in the definition of a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: Tag 0HA5 (lemma-locally-G-scheme), (3) implies (2); the G-ring definition is More on Algebra Tag 07GH (definition-G-ring).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-j2-affine-cover] to the locally Noetherian scheme $X$ of step 1 and the same affine cover. Every $A_i$ is J-2 by step 1, so its conclusion says that $B$ is J-2. This is the open-regular-locus condition for all finite type $B$-algebras, not merely openness of the regular locus of $B$ itself.

source.place: Tag 07R4 (lemma-J), (4) implies (3), as used in the quasi-excellent case of Tag 0HAB (lemma-locally-excellent).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-universally-catenary-affine-cover] to the locally Noetherian scheme $X$ of step 1. The hypothesis holds on the same cover because every $A_i$ is universally catenary. The conclusion is that $B$ is universally catenary.

source.place: Tag 02J9 (lemma-universally-catenary-local), (4) implies (3), as used in the excellent case of Tag 0HAB (lemma-locally-excellent).

proof.text: The ring $B$ is Noetherian and a G-ring by step 2, J-2 by step 3, and universally catenary by step 4. The first three predicates say precisely that $B$ is quasi-excellent, and adding universal catenarity says precisely that $B$ is excellent, by [def-exc-excellent-ring]. As $V$ was arbitrary, this proves the first assertion.

source.place: Tag 0HAB (lemma-locally-excellent), proof using Tag 0HAA (lemma-characterize-excellent); ring definition is More on Algebra Tag 07QT (definition-excellent).

proof.text: Let $W\subseteq X$ be any open subscheme. For each $x\in W$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] supplies an affine open $V$ of $X$ with $x\in V\subseteq W$. Hence the collection of all affine opens $V\subseteq W$ covers $W$. By step 5 each $\mathcal O_X(V)$ is excellent, and the restricted structure sheaf of the open subscheme satisfies $\mathcal O_W(V)=\mathcal O_X(V)$ [def-pc-scheme]. These same opens are the required affine cover of $W$. If $W$ is empty, the empty collection is already a cover.

source.place: Tag 0HAB (lemma-locally-excellent), final assertion; Schemes Tag 01IT (schemes.tex, lemma-basis-affine-opens).
